changed.title: The 5 by 5 bipartite graph with mask 3320506 is represented on the one-a-side promise by an AND/OR/NOT circuit of fan-in two with at most 10 gates
changed.statement: ∃ C : PEqualNP.CircuitLowerBounds.Circuit, PEqualNP.MetaComplexity.FanInTwo C ∧ C.size ≤ 10 ∧ PEqualNP.Represents.Represents (fun u v : Fin 5 => (3320506 : ℕ).testBit (5 * u.val + v.val)) C
changed.unlocks: Whether a NOT gate pays under a checked AND/OR floor of 11 on a side-5 graph with no twin class and no single line to negate; a yes would be a kind of saving we have not seen.
changed.sketch: We hold no circuit of 10 gates; this is a search. We see no class of equal rows or columns here and no single line whose negation would pay; a yes would be a kind of saving we have not seen. Give a gate list of AND, OR and NOT gates of fan-in two, at most 10 gates, judged by evaluation on the 25 promise inputs. The graph needs at least 11 AND/OR gates by a checked floor row (search 'mask 3320506'). An exhausted search is a report, not a proof.

changed.title: A split of a two-round cyclic output parity forces one key block to vanish at each selected pair of coordinates
changed.unlocks: restricts which key subspaces can supply two selected coordinates at each output bit
changed.context: The initial mix is invertible by the period-three recurrence and the spacing-two square identity. Use the initial mixed state as coordinates. Reinjection is affine there. A parity computed as two local functions has zero mixed difference across the two blocks at every base. Take both endpoint differences. The resulting determinant vanishes on the two projected blocks, which together span the two-bit plane, so one projection is zero. For total parity the pairs form the step-2d cycle, connected at odd k. Ownership agrees at every shared vertex.

changed.title: A perfect matching in 6-vertex graphs, on 15 edge bits: an AND/OR/NOT circuit of fan-in at most two with at most 30 gates
changed.unlocks: a calibration of our constructions for this function
changed.context: Answer with a circuit, not an argument: a gate list (operation, wires read; wires 0 to n-1 are the input bits in the order the statement names, gate j writes wire n+j, each gate reads only earlier wires) and the output wire. Judged by one kernel evaluation over every input. A calibration of our constructions; no claim attached either way. We hold 34 gates (no NOT gate), built as vertex 0 matched to each other vertex in turn, the matchings of the remaining four vertices shared; we do not know whether 30 exists. 15 inputs: use the column replay pattern.

changed.title: One-a-side promise: the 4 by 5 bipartite graph with mask 34940 has a fan-in-two AND/OR circuit of at most 8 gates
changed.statement: PEqualNP.Represents.RepSizeAtMost (fun (u : Fin 4) (v : Fin 5) => (34940 : ℕ).testBit (5 * u.val + v.val)) 8
changed.unlocks: the AND/OR cost of 4 by 5 graphs off the square, where the checked twin merge sends square graphs, for the silent-line work
changed.sketch: A search unit. We hold a circuit of 9 AND/OR gates (three plain forms, full lines taken out and equal gates merged); at this size those forms are weak; we hold none of 8; this is a search. Our count of unread rows and columns gives a floor of 8 (on paper), a gap of 1. Answer with a gate list (AND or OR, each reading at most two wires; wires 0 to 3 left, 4 to 8 right, gate j writes wire 9 + j, each gate reading only earlier wires) and its output wire, judged on all 20 inputs with one vertex on each side.

changed.title: The two-lit function of the graph H on 6 points with mask 270715563 on shared wires has an AND/OR/NOT circuit of fan-in two with at most 9 gates
changed.statement: ∃ C : PEqualNP.CircuitLowerBounds.Circuit, PEqualNP.MetaComplexity.FanInTwo C ∧ C.size ≤ 9 ∧ ∀ i j : Fin 6, C.eval (List.ofFn fun k : Fin 6 => decide (k = i ∨ k = j)) = (270715563 : ℕ).testBit (6 * min i.val j.val + max i.val j.val)
changed.unlocks: the exact size of the two-lit-points function of this graph on six shared wires; the family shows where a NOT gate pays with no equal lines
changed.sketch: We hold a circuit of 10 gates, a weak hand form (best over a few point orders and the complement plus a NOT, equal gates merged): OR(0,1), OR(2,6), NOT(7), AND(5,8), OR(3,7), AND(4,10), AND(2,6), OR(9,11), OR(12,13), NOT(14) (inputs 0-5 are the points, gate k is wire 6 + k, output last). We hold no circuit of 9 gates; this is a search. No complete search of ours has run at six points.
